questions.q: Describe the three-tier structure of the Panchayati Raj system.
answer: Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government in rural areas, organised in three tiers so that decisions can be taken at village, block and district levels.

answer.text: At the village level, it is the elected body that looks after the day-to-day needs of one or a few villages.
At the intermediate or block level (also called Mandal), it coordinates the work of several Gram Panchayats.
At the district level, it oversees and plans development for the whole district.

answer: The system was given constitutional status by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment of 1992.

questions.q: What is the Gram Sabha, and why is it important for grassroots democracy?
answer: The Gram Sabha is the assembly of all adult voters of a village or panchayat area, and it is the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system.

answer.text: Because every voter can attend and speak, the Gram Sabha allows people to take part directly in decisions about their own village — a form of direct democracy at the grassroots.
It discusses the village's needs, approves development plans and budgets, and reviews the work of the Gram Panchayat.
By questioning the elected Gram Panchayat, the Gram Sabha keeps it answerable to the people, which is why it is called the watchdog of grassroots democracy.

questions.q: Describe the structure and functions of the Gram Panchayat.

answer.text: The Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body of the village. Its head is the Sarpanch (or Pradhan), its members are the Panch elected from different wards, and an appointed Panchayat Secretary keeps records and helps run it. It is elected for a term of five years, with seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women.

It provides basic services such as drinking water, village roads, street lighting, drainage and sanitation; maintains records of births and deaths; supports local schools and health work; helps settle local disputes; and carries out development works using local taxes and government grants.

answer: In this way the Gram Panchayat turns the decisions of the Gram Sabha into action for the village.
